SimuLean Core — API Reference

Every public and protected type of the discrete-event simulation core (Assets/SimuLean.Net/). Generated directly from the C# sources and their XML documentation comments, so it never drifts from the code. The Unity integration and the GA optimization module are deliberately out of scope — they consume this API.

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimClock/ActionEvent.cs:23

: IEvent

Marks an event that never moves items by itself — a calendar / shift tick, the next failure of an MTBF generator, a timetable stop start, the warm-up reset. While only such events remain the model cannot progress unless an element is stopped (its stop's end is a normal event): the clock raises imClock.Idle for the run monitor (model empty / deadlock).

No public or protected members.

struct ParameterValue A typed, allocation-free parameter value: exactly one of int / double / bool / string, tagged by ind. Replaces the former boxed object in the per-model parameter bag…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimClock/ParameterValue.cs:38

: IEquatable<ParameterValue>

A typed, allocation-free parameter value: exactly one of int / double / bool / string, tagged by ind. Replaces the former boxed object in the per-model parameter bag (imContext.ModelParameters). Efficiency: this is a readonly struct . Numeric kinds (int/double/bool) share a single ouble field and never allocate; only the string kind carries a reference. Storing it in a Dictionary<string,ParameterValue> therefore boxes nothing, unlike the previous Dictionary<string,object> which boxed every numeric/boolean value. Use the implicit conversions to build values ( ParameterValue p = 3; , = 2.5; , = true; , = "round_robin"; ) and the strongly typed As* accessors (throw on kind mismatch) or the non-throwing TryGet* methods to read them back.

Properties

bool IsNoneTrue when this value carries no payload.
ParameterKind KindWhich of the payload slots is meaningful for this value.

enum RunEndReason Why a run ended.

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimClock/RunStatus.cs:6

Why a run ended.

Values

HorizonStill running, or ran to its horizon (max time).
StopAtCountThe end condition's elements ( StopAt : sinks, or any elements) received the end count.
EmptyNothing left to do: no event can move items and no item waits (sources exhausted, model empty).
DeadlockStopped on a deadlock (with the end condition "when empty").
StalledStopped when items were left waiting with nothing able to happen, none blocked (end condition "when empty").
FinishedNothing left to do with items still in the model: at rest in buffers without outputs (the finished product) or surplus no element will take (an unlimited source behind a full rack) — end condition "when empty".

The state of a run as the run monitor sees it (imContext.Run): why it ended and when, and whether it stalled — no event can move items while items wait in elements that are not stopped (a kit that will never be complete, stock left at the end) — or deadlocked : stalled with an element blocked or waiting for a resource. Read by the results ( RunResults , scope model ).

Properties

double DeadlockTimeTime of the first deadlock (NaN = none).

double EndTimeTime the end condition stopped the run (NaN = not stopped).
double FinishTimeTime nothing was left to do (NaN = never): empty, or every item left at rest in a buffer without outputs or surplus no element will take. Not a stall.

double StallTimeTime the run stalled (NaN = never).

class SimCalendar Maps simulation time (a unit-less double owned by imClock) to calendar dates and back. One calendar per model, owned by imContext.Calendar. The engine keeps simulating in plain…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimClock/SimCalendar.cs:19

Maps simulation time (a unit-less double owned by imClock) to calendar dates and back. One calendar per model, owned by imContext.Calendar. The engine keeps simulating in plain numbers; the calendar is only a view: date = Start + simTime · SecondsPerUnit . It is used to convert date-stamped input data (order books, downtime traces, shift patterns) to sim time at load time, and to format sim time for reports. Immutable and thread-safe. Dates are treated as local "wall clock" time with no time zone or daylight-saving adjustment (a plant calendar).

class SimClock SimClock simulates the clock of the simulation: one clock per model and per run (a new run builds its model on a new clock). It is independent of the Unity clock. The clock owns the…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimClock/SimClock.cs:10

SimClock simulates the clock of the simulation: one clock per model and per run (a new run builds its model on a new clock). It is independent of the Unity clock. The clock owns the model's imContext (element registry + seeded random streams); construct it with a seed for reproducible runs.

Constructors

SimClock()No summary in source.
SimClock(int? seed)Creates a clock whose imContext derives all random streams from seed. Pass null for a distinct nondeterministic seed.

Properties

SimContext ContextPer-model context: element registry and seeded random streams.
long EventsExecutedEvents executed since the clock was created (performance measurements: events per second).
int ForegroundEventCountPending events that can move items (not BackgroundEvents).
bool IsStoppedTrue once top was called.
int PendingEventCountNumber of pending (non-cancelled) events.
double StopTimeSimulation time at which the run was stopped (NaN while running).

Methods

bool AdvanceClock(double time)Advances sim time until time, executing every pending (non-cancelled) event in (time, insertion-order) sequence, then leaves the clock AT time (so time-weighted statistics and open state intervals are measured up to the requested horizon). Returns false when no events remain.
System.DateTime GetDateTime()Calendar date of the current simulation time (see imContext.Calendar).
double GetSimulationTime()Returns current simulation time in seconds.
EventHandle Schedule(System.Action action, double delay)Schedules action after delay (a one-off ctionEvent). Timed work of an element goes through lement.ScheduleWork instead, so downtime can pause it.
EventHandle ScheduleEvent(IEvent theEvent, double time)Default method to schedule an theEvent at time (time + simTime). Returns a handle that can cancel the event before it fires; reschedule = Cancel() + ScheduleEvent again.
void Stop()Ends the run now (an end condition was met): dvanceClock returns at once and from then on does not move the clock, so the statistics are measured up to topTime.

Events

System.Action IdleRaised when no event that can move items is left (only BackgroundEvents, or none): after an event, and when dvanceClock starts. The run monitor tells an empty model from a deadlock.
class SimContext Per-model simulation context owned by a imClock. Replaces the former process-wide static element registry so that many models (e.g. parallel headless GA evaluations) can coexist without…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimClock/SimContext.cs:15

Per-model simulation context owned by a imClock. Replaces the former process-wide static element registry so that many models (e.g. parallel headless GA evaluations) can coexist without sharing state, and provides the model's random streams: one per stochastic source, each derived from the model seed and the source's stable key (owner element name + purpose), see reateRandomStream(string, string).

Properties

SimCalendar CalendarCalendar that maps simulation time to dates (start date + seconds per unit). Defaults to imCalendar.Default; set it before building date-driven data (order books, downtime traces, shifts).
SimClock ClockThe clock this context belongs to.
SimuLean.Data.ModelData DataThe model's named data tables: the snapshot taken at the run's start, read-only.
System.Collections.Generic.ISet<System.DateTime> HolidaysThe model's holidays (dates): the working calendar shared by every shift — a shift pattern skips them as it skips its own. Set before building the shifts.
Dictionary<string, ParameterValue> ModelParametersPer-model parameters accessible to output-routing strategies (formerly the process-wide static GeneralLink.GlobalModelParameters ). Kept per-context so parallel headless models never share routing state. Populate before a run; eneralLink passes it into every OutputStrategyContext . Values are typed arameterValues (int / double / bool / string) rather than boxed object , so numeric/boolean parameters never allocate.
IRandomEngine RandomEngineThe context's root random engine (thread-safe, seeded with eed). Shared by everything that uses it, so draws depend on call order — model elements should use their own stream (reateRandomStream(string, string)) instead.
RunStatus RunHow the run is going / ended: end condition, end reason, deadlock (set by the run monitor).
int SeedModel seed of this run. Every random stream derives from it (and from its owner's key). A clock built without a seed draws a fresh one (ewRandomSeed); read it here to reproduce the run ( new SimClock(seed) or eseed).
SimuLean.Signals.SignalHub SignalsThe model's signal table: subscriptions made when the model is built; created on first use, so a model without reactions has none.
SimuLean.Signals.SignalHub SignalsIfAnyThe signal table if the model has one, else null (for views: reading it creates nothing).

Methods

T AssignRandomStream<T>(T sampler, string owner, string purpose = null)Gives sampler its own stream (reateRandomStream(string, string)) when it draws random numbers (RandomStreamUser); deterministic samplers (constants, label expressions) are returned untouched and consume no key.
IRandomEngine CreateRandomStream(string owner, string purpose = null)Creates the random stream of one stochastic source: seeded with eriveStreamSeed(eed, key), key = owner/purpose (e.g. "Lathe/delay" , "Src/interArrival" ). The key, not the creation order, decides the numbers, so adding or removing other elements does not change what this source draws (common random numbers), and the Unity scene and a headless rebuild of the same model draw the same numbers per source. A key requested again since the last (re)seed — several slots of one element, elements with the same name — gets key#1 , key#2 … in request order.
  • owner — Stable identity of the owner, normally the element name.
  • purpose — What the stream samples ( delay , interArrival , ttf …).

: Element, SimuLean.Resources.IResourceUser

Assembly workstation executing a precedence network (a small CPM graph) of tasks per job. A job item arrives on the main input; materials arrive in a shared kuStockPort and are matched by SKU. Up to workerCount tasks run concurrently. A task becomes READY at the first instant its predecessors are complete AND its materials are in stock; dispatch order is first-ready-first, tie-broken by descending ssemblyTaskSpec.Priority then declaration order. Consumed materials are attached to the job as sub-items; when every task has completed the job is sent onward.

class Delay An activity without capacity: every item that enters waits its own delay, drawn when it enters (an expression reads the item, e.g. t_test ), all at once — a patient at home for a night,…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimElements/Delay.cs:14

: Element

An activity without capacity: every item that enters waits its own delay, drawn when it enters (an expression reads the item, e.g. t_test ), all at once — a patient at home for a night, three months on a therapy, a curing time, a transit. Its cost does not depend on how many items wait (a ultiServer with a huge capacity was the workaround). The delays are work of the element (lement.ScheduleWork): an Immediate stop pauses them. An item whose delay is over and that cannot leave waits, in the order they finished, until the output frees (state BLOCKED when nothing else is running).

struct ElementState A typed, interned element-state token. Replaces the former loose string state (and the string-constant ElementState class): setting an element's state now goes through…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimElements/ElementState.cs:30

: IEquatable<ElementState>

A typed, interned element-state token. Replaces the former loose string state (and the string-constant ElementState class): setting an element's state now goes through lement.SetState, which is the single point that updates the state statistics (lementStateTracker). Closed core set, open extension. The engine defines a small predefined set (DLE, ECEIVING, ROCESSING, LOCKED, RAVELLING, AITING_FOR_RESOURCE). Subsystems that need their own states (e.g. resources: TRAVELLING_EMPTY / LOADING / TRAVELLING_LOADED / UNLOADING) obtain a token via f, which interns by name so equal names always resolve to the same value. This gives a limited, predefined vocabulary for the common cases while still allowing subsystem-specific states — chosen over a plain enum for exactly that reason. The token is a readonly struct carrying only the interned ame reference, so it is cheap to copy and compare. The ame is the stable string that surfaces in reports / CSV / the Unity inspector, so existing outputs are unchanged.

class LengthLimitedQueue Accumulation lane(s) limited by length instead of item count: roller or chain conveyor buffers, floor lanes, gravity lanes. Each item occupies its own length plus a ap to the item in…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimElements/LengthLimitedQueue.cs:33

: Element

Accumulation lane(s) limited by length instead of item count: roller or chain conveyor buffers, floor lanes, gravity lanes. Each item occupies its own length plus a ap to the item in front; one element can model several parallel lanes that share an entry and an exit (e.g. a multi-lane accumulation buffer). Item length. Taken, in this order, from temLength (a strategy delegate), the numeric item label engthLabel (default "length" ), or efaultItemLength. Units are whatever the model uses (metres by convention). Entry. An item goes to the first lane (lowest index) where the occupied length + ap + its length fits the lane length. With cceptOversizeOnEmptyLane (default true) an empty lane always takes one item, however long, so an item longer than every lane cannot deadlock the flow. axItems adds an optional count limit. Exit. Global FIFO. Each lane is FIFO and items are assigned in arrival order, so the oldest item is always at the front of its lane: global FIFO equals the physical per-lane order. An item that can pass straight through (lane empty and the downstream element accepts it) never occupies a lane, as in temsQueue. Statistics are driven by the Link layer only (every item crosses the element's input/output links); the element only sets its state (IDLE / PROCESSING when holding items / BLOCKED when the output refused its head item). There is no transit time: combine it with a ultiServer if the conveyor travel time matters. Engine-pure (no Unity dependency). See docs/architecture.md §3.13.

: SingleJobStation

Picking / kitting station. A container (order) item arrives on the main input; stock items of various SKUs accumulate in a kuStockPort. The pick list (SKU → qty) for each container is resolved through an PickListSource chain (e.g. SQLite table → container labels → static table). When the whole list is satisfiable from stock the station picks the items into the container (as sub-items), processes for a sampled delay, and sends the container out (one container at a time, ingleJobStation, optional resources). AFTER each completed pick cycle, all remaining (non-picked) stock is flushed in batch through the eturnsPort.

class ReleaseSource A source driven by external logic: controllers (planners, order-release rules, initial-stock loaders) nqueue ready-made items, and the source pushes them downstream in FIFO order as soon…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimElements/ReleaseSource.cs:17

: Element

A source driven by external logic: controllers (planners, order-release rules, initial-stock loaders) nqueue ready-made items, and the source pushes them downstream in FIFO order as soon as the downstream element accepts them. When downstream is full the head item waits and is retried on the standard nblock notification, so a finite downstream buffer acts as a kanban limit on released work. Items leave through the output link, so statistics are recorded as for any other element (content stays 0, see tatistics.ElementStatsCollector.TracksContent). Pending (not yet released) items are counted by endingCount, not as content.

A station that works on one job at a time and gathers what the job needs before processing it (Combiner: components; PickingStation: picked stock). One cycle: the job item arrives ( RECEIVING , nJobArrived); the subclass gathers and calls tartJob; the resources are acquired ( WAITING_FOR_RESOURCE , optional esources); it processes for the sampled delay ( PROCESSING , nProcessingStarted); the job is sent out — or waits ( BLOCKED ) until nblock sends it; then the slot is freed and the resources released (nJobLeaving, nJobLeft). The element's state is the slot's, so utilisation is the time share PROCESSING.

class Stacker Stacker / palletiser: receives items of any type and builds stacks at N positions, then releases each finished stack downstream as one compound item that carries the stacked items as…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimElements/Stacker.cs:151

: Element, SimuLean.Resources.IResourceUser

Stacker / palletiser: receives items of any type and builds stacks at N positions, then releases each finished stack downstream as one compound item that carries the stacked items as tem.subItems (the engine's batching convention, as the combiner and the picking / assembly stations use it). Generalised from a pick-and-place board stacker of an industrial application; nothing in it depends on the item type. Flow. The stacker has one pick point (capacity 1): an item arriving there waits until a position can take it, then a pick-and-place cycle moves it onto the stack (duration sampled from ycleTime, scheduled with lement.ScheduleWork so stops pause it; null = instantaneous, still as a separate same-time event). The pick point is freed when the cycle starts, so the next item can arrive while the gantry places the current one. One cycle at a time. Positions and capacity. apacity items per position (or the position's own tackPosition.Capacity) and optionally a height limit axHeight using the item height (temHeight delegate → numeric label eightLabel → efaultItemHeight). A stack completes when it reaches its capacity, or when another item as high as the one just placed would exceed the height limit; eleaseStack / eleaseAll close a partial stack on demand (end of batch, control logic). The position is chosen by electionRule or the ositionSelector delegate. With eleasePartialWhenBlocked (default) an item that cannot be placed because open stacks are in its way (its stack is too high for it, or all positions hold other keys) closes the blocking stack — the oldest one when several qualify — so the stacker cannot deadlock. Release. A complete stack becomes a new item of type tackType (labels of its first item copied when opyLabelsFromFirst, plus stackPosition , stackCount , stackHeight , stackKey and stackReason ) and is sent through the output link; refused stacks wait in completion order and are retried on nblock. The position is free again once its stack has left. Statistics come only from the Link layer: every stacked item enters through the input link, and the compound leaves through the output link. The stacker opts in to tatistics.ElementStatsCollector.CountSubItemsOnExit, so the compound's exit records each stacked item as leaving (input = output = items, exact content and stay times); downstream elements count the compound as one item. States: PROCESSING (cycle running), BLOCKED (a complete stack cannot leave, or the waiting item cannot be placed), RECEIVING (stacks forming, waiting for items), IDLE (empty). Views get C# events (temArrived, ycleStarted, temPlaced, tackCompleted, tackReleased) plus the VElement calls. Engine-pure (no Unity dependency). See docs/architecture.md §3.14.

class ListLink Connects elements to a imList: it is the output link of the elements that push their items to the list and the input link of the elements that pull from it. Push. Every distinct item…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimLink/ListLink.cs:28

: ILink

Connects elements to a imList: it is the output link of the elements that push their items to the list and the input link of the elements that pull from it. Push. Every distinct item an origin offers (endItem) — whatever the element — is advertised once in the list and stays in the origin, which sees a refused send and keeps it (blocked, as with a full destination). Offering an advertised item again (the origin retrying, e.g. after a stop) re-evaluates the pending pulls. Entries of a stopped origin are not matched until it resumes. Pull. A puller with free capacity registers a pull with its query (plus its input strategy); when an entry matches, the item is reserved for it and its origin hands over that very item (lement.SendHeldItem, after the current event), which transfers it. The transfer fires OnExit / OnEntry like eneralLink, so statistics stay link-driven. Call tart after the elements' own Start (registers the first pulls). Transport. When the holder carries its items with resources (etTransport, its transportBy , as FlexSim's Use Transport ), the reserved item is not handed over at once: a carrier is requested (esources.TransportMoves), travels to the holder, loads (the item leaves the holder), travels to the puller and delivers (the item enters it). The reservation keeps the puller from pulling another item meanwhile ("in transit").

class WalkLink Output link of an element whose items walk by themselves to the next element (the item is a mobile entity — a patient walks, as Simio's entities on paths or AnyLogic's MoveTo ; the staff…

SimuLean  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/SimLink/WalkLink.cs:40

: ILink

Output link of an element whose items walk by themselves to the next element (the item is a mobile entity — a patient walks, as Simio's entities on paths or AnyLogic's MoveTo ; the staff stay resources). The walk uses the resources' travel models (TravelModel: the transport network, a walk grid, a travel matrix) and their animation contract (ravelLeg), so a patient and an operator move alike. When the origin offers an item, a destination is chosen as the transport link does: the origin's output strategy among the destinations that can take it, counting the items already on their way to each. The item leaves the origin ( OnExit , its exit labels) and walks from the origin's lement.Location to the destination's in the planned time — model time — then enters it ( Receive , OnEntry , its entry labels): statistics stay link-driven; the walk is in neither element (a sink's age includes it). If the destination cannot take it on arrival (another input filled it, a stop), it waits at its door until it can. Two elements without a location, or at the same one, hand the item over at once (a general link). No resource and no capacity on the way; the elements' stops do not pause a walk.

SimuLean.Statistics  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Statistics/StatTimeWeightedVariable.cs:14

: StatVariable

Tracks a level over simulation time and reports its TIME-WEIGHTED average: the integral of the level over time divided by the observed span. Use for content / WIP / queue-length variables, where the average must account for how LONG the level held each value, not how many times it changed. The statistics family: - tatLevelVariable — event counters (input/output totals). - tatTally — independent observations (stay times, waits). - tatTimeWeightedVariable — levels integrated over time (this class).

The transport network: nodes + typed tracks, shared by all transport modes. Provides shortest-path routing (Dijkstra) and total distance between any two nodes, optionally restricted to a set of track types (e.g. vehicles route over TravelPath tracks only). Deterministic: same network + same query → same path (ties broken by node-id ordinal). Routes are cached per (from, to, mode) and the cache is invalidated on any topology edit; topology is expected to be static during a run. Engine-side and Unity-free: coordinates/lengths are resolved by the caller (Unity layer or config) before or while building the network.

class StorageSystem A first-class storage element (proposal §4): a set of parametric torageLanes, a stock list of the stored items (a private imList: retrievals are list queries), pluggable location /…

SimuLean.Storage  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Storage/StorageSystem.cs:38

: Element

A first-class storage element (proposal §4): a set of parametric torageLanes, a stock list of the stored items (a private imList: retrievals are list queries), pluggable location / relocation policies, and optional timed moves by resources (its ransport use: a team of cranes, forklifts, operators). Flow put-away arrives through the standard input Link (eceive); retrievals are requested programmatically via equestRetrieval and leave through the standard output link when one is connected, so link-driven statistics stay correct. v1 simplifications (documented by design): - Relocation moves are strictly sequential (each blocker move is issued in the previous move's arrival callback); concurrent-crane optimization is out of scope. - Blocker destinations are planned atomically up-front: if any blocker has no valid home the retrieval fails with no state change. In transport mode the plan is not revised mid-flight, and overlapping retrievals from the same lane are not supported. - When no transport team is set — or a lane / the storage has no node (lement.Location) — the move is instantaneous at the current simulation time. Retrieved items are carried to the storage's own location (its outbound point). An unreachable node fails loudly. - No deferred put-away queue: the upstream element holds rejected items and retries (standard protocol). - A retrieved item the output does not take at once waits at the outbound point, still in the storage (its nblock / endHeldItem send it when the receiver has room or a carrier loads it). Overlapping retrievals never fetch the same item; a lane being emptied takes no put-away and the places planned for relocated blockers are reserved.

Blockers in front of the target are re-homed by the relocation policy; destinations are planned atomically before anything moves. With a transport system, blocker moves and the final target move are chained sequentially at realistic times; otherwise everything happens instantly at the current simulation time. When the target finally leaves it is delivered through the output link if one is connected (so exit/entry statistics fire normally), and onRetrieved is invoked. Returns false when no item matches or a blocker cannot be re-homed (no state is changed in that case).

class ModelList<T> A FlexSim-style model list: a decoupling rendezvous between producers (Push) and consumers (Pull) of any model object — items, move requests, vehicles, orders. The essential feature is…

SimuLean.Collections  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Collections/ModelList.cs:25

A FlexSim-style model list: a decoupling rendezvous between producers (Push) and consumers (Pull) of any model object — items, move requests, vehicles, orders. The essential feature is back-orders : a Pull with no matching entry registers a back-order; a later Push that matches it fulfills the pull directly (the value never enters the list). This makes "idle transporter waits for work" and "work waits for a transporter" symmetric without bespoke wiring. Determinism: entries and back-orders carry a monotone sequence number. With no sort, pulls are FIFO by insertion; back-orders are always fulfilled oldest-first among those whose filter matches. No wall-clock, no unordered iteration — safe for reproducible simulation runs. Not thread-safe by design: it lives inside a single model's event loop (one SimClock), like every other engine structure.

int CountNumber of stored (unpulled) entries.

Returns the back-order, or null when the pull was satisfied at once.
bool Push(T value)Pushes a value. If a registered back-order's filter matches, the oldest such back-order is fulfilled immediately and the value never enters the list; otherwise the value is stored. Returns true if the push fulfilled a back-order.

bool TryPull(Func<T, bool> filter, Comparison<T> sort, out T value)Attempts an immediate pull. Selects among entries matching filter (null = all); with a sort, the best-ranked entry wins (ties broken by insertion order), otherwise FIFO. Returns false if nothing matches.

SimuLean.Collections  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Collections/SimList.cs:22

A FlexSim-style list: a model-wide rendezvous where elements and model logic push entries (items they hold — the item does not move —, or values) and pull them with a istQuery. A pull with no match becomes a back-order and is delivered by a zero-delay event at the time a matching entry is pushed (so the pusher finishes its own event first). Built on odelList{T}; deterministic. Fields of an entry, for filters and orders: the item's labels (numeric or text), the value entry's push-time fields, and the built-ins age (now − push time), pushTime , itemPriority , owner (owner name) and type (item type), plus named calculated fields (efineField). Field access is the only place to change when items get a property bag. Statistics: content (time-weighted), waiting time per pulled entry, pushes / pulls, pending pulls (time-weighted).

class RunMonitor Run control of a built model, installed by eadlessModelFactory.StartModel — so scene runs and headless runs honour it alike: end condition — stop when the elements…

SimuLean.Headless  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Serialization/RunMonitor.cs:36

Run control of a built model, installed by eadlessModelFactory.StartModel — so scene runs and headless runs honour it alike: end condition — stop when the elements imulationConfig.StopAt (sinks, or the buffers that hold the finished product) have received imulationConfig.StopAtCount items between them, and / or when nothing is left to do (imulationConfig.StopWhenEmpty); the clock stops (imClock.Stop) and the statistics end there; empty / finished / stalled / deadlock — when no event that can move items is left (imClock.Idle), the items still in the model are sorted out: at rest : in a buffer (queue, lane) without outputs — the finished product, not waiting; surplus : ready to leave, but every element downstream is empty (or holds surplus itself) — no element will ever take them, e.g. an unlimited source blocked behind a full rack whose consumers are done (#26); starved : components in a Combiner with no main item while its main input's supply is exhausted (every element upstream of the main input is empty — at Idle no source will create anything more): they wait for material that will never come, which is not a deadlock (#28); waiting : the others. No item at all = empty ; none waiting = finished (not a stall); waiting = stalled (logged; an element under a stop is no exception: at Idle no event is left to end the stop); stalled with an item ready to leave that is not surplus — an element BLOCKED or WAITING_FOR_RESOURCE, or a buffer with outputs, behind an element that holds items — = deadlock (warned once). Each waiting element is named with what it waits for, and the outcome is flagged in imContext.Run. sTerminal (no outputs) also gives the results their makespan: the last entry into a terminal element. Read-only towards the model (it moves nothing, schedules nothing).

Flat-list encoding of transport/storage configuration data inside lementConfig.Parameters (unified proposal §8). Everything is a List<string> of pipe-delimited records: node : "id|x|y|z" track: "fromId|toId|length|bidirectional|trackType" (length < 0 = auto/euclidean) lane : "laneId|x|y|z|capacity|accessDiscipline|skuConstraint|nodeId" (nodeId may be empty) Rationale: no tuple-keyed dictionaries (JSON-hostile), and the GA's in-memory CloneConfig already deep-clones List<string> values, so parallel evaluations never share mutable state. All numbers use InvariantCulture round-trip format. Ids containing '|' are sanitized to '_' at encode time.

Keep engine code free of Unity dependencies — callers supply the file path (the Unity layer resolves the default under the project root).

Tables a source reads when its model is built (headless, in a scene run, in a Study), instead of a copy kept in the scene — so every run reads the same, current data (SQL as the source of data). A table spec is one of: sql:<SELECT …> — a query of the project database (columns as returned: Name , Time , Q and labels for a Schedule source); naval:<part>[;interval=h][;start=h][;lead=h]:<table, SELECT … or file> — a part ( subblocks , blocks , erection ) generated from a block breakdown (imuLean.Naval.BlockBreakdown), released every interval in erection order from start , the sub-block kits lead before their block. The spec is a catalog key of the source ( tableSource ), so a Study varies it like a file (ship variants as scenarios); the database path is resolved by the caller (the Unity layer: the project database by default).

A generator drives lement.Stop/lement.Resume on one target element, so it works with any element; what "stopped" means for the element (pause its work, refuse items) is defined by lement and its lement.ScheduleWork usage. class PeriodicDowntime A repeating planned stop: every eriod the target stops for uration, the first stop at irst, optionally only stops that start before ntil (preventive maintenance, a break every shift, a…

SimuLean.Downtime  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Downtime/DowntimeGenerators.cs:247

: DowntimeGenerator

A repeating planned stop: every eriod the target stops for uration, the first stop at irst, optionally only stops that start before ntil (preventive maintenance, a break every shift, a cleaning cycle). Absolute times on the model clock, like a timetable: one start event is pending at a time (the next stop is scheduled when the current one starts; nothing is materialised up front). A start after irst skips the stops already over and applies a running one for its remaining part. Defaults: state SCHEDULED_DOWN, mode Immediate. Invalid settings throw rgumentException at construction.

class ShiftDowntime Stops the element outside the working windows of a weekly shift pattern, using the model imCalendar. Defaults: state OFF_SHIFT, mode AfterCurrent (work in progress finishes, no new items…

SimuLean.Downtime  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Downtime/DowntimeGenerators.cs:475

: DowntimeGenerator

Stops the element outside the working windows of a weekly shift pattern, using the model imCalendar. Defaults: state OFF_SHIFT, mode AfterCurrent (work in progress finishes, no new items are taken). The end of a working window takes effect a hair early (loseTolerance): a job that ends at the closing time up to rounding must not let the next item start before the stop (13 patients in a 12-slot session). Two roundings meet there: the drift of slot times summed from the window's start, and slot lengths typed in single precision (the Unity fields are float : 20 min as 0.3333333 h is 0.12 ms short, so twelve slots end 1.4 ms early).

class Expression The SimuLean expression syntax — one syntax for every decision a property can drive: process / cycle times, request priorities, routing, admission conditions, list fields. Parsed once,…

SimuLean.Expressions  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Expressions/Expression.cs:101

The SimuLean expression syntax — one syntax for every decision a property can drive: process / cycle times, request priorities, routing, admission conditions, list fields. Parsed once, evaluated many times without allocating. Values: numbers 12 , 3.5 ; texts 'red' or "red" . Properties: item.weight , element.speed ( station.speed is the same), item['any name'] ; a bare weight is the context's default (the item for times and priorities, the entry's field in a list). Built-in values when no property has that name: item.id , item.type , item.priority , item.created , item.age ; element.name , element.content , element.free . A missing value counts as 0 (or as no text). Operators: + - * / % , comparisons == != < <= > >= (texts compare with == / != ; a true comparison is 1), && || ! , cond ? a : b , parentheses. Functions: min max abs floor ceil round sqrt pow if(c, a, b) now() has(item.x) ; random (from the element's stream, RandomScope): rand() (0–1), uniform(a, b) , exponential(mean) , normal(mean, sd) , pick(w1, v1, w2, v2, …) (a value with probability proportional to its weight); other elements by name (ModelScope): content('X') , free('X') , get('X', 'property') . Data tables (the model's named tables, SimContext.Data ): table('t', key, 'col') — the cell of the first row whose first column equals key ( table('t', key, 'col', 'keyCol') for another key column; a number matches a cell of the same value, 3 = '3.0' ); cell('t', row, 'col') (rows from 1); rows('t') / rows('t', 'col', value) (how many / how many with that value); sum('t', 'col') / sum('t', 'col', 'keyCol', key) . A cell that reads as a number is a number, else a text; no such row (or an empty cell) is a missing value (0). An unknown table or column fails, naming it.

class Agenda An appointment book: a patient that enters (a referral) is booked into the first free slot of the agenda's sessions at least eadTime ahead, waits in the agenda (at home) and is released…

SimuLean.Healthcare  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Healthcare/Agenda.cs:34

: Element

An appointment book: a patient that enters (a referral) is booked into the first free slot of the agenda's sessions at least eadTime ahead, waits in the agenda (at home) and is released at its appointment time to the next element (the consultation). Sessions are a weekly pattern (eeklyShiftPattern, e.g. Mon-Fri 08:30-12:30 ) cut into slots of lotLength, on the model calendar with the model's holidays (I7) and the agenda's own. The first eservedPerSession slots of every session are kept for priority patients (riorityLabel ≠ 0); verflow says what they do when none is free. A oShow probability (an expression over the patient, drawn from the agenda's stream) marks no_show at the appointment — routing decides what happens next. Labels stamped: booked_at , appt_time , lead_time , no_show . With load < 1 the waits are those of the booking (weeks), not of a server (hours). The visit station needs no shift: the agenda releases patients at their slot times.

The product structure of a ship's hull for a block-assembly / erection model : one row per sub-block — its block, kind, turning, dimensions, work content per stage, the block's erection order or predecessors and its place on the hull. Read from SQL (the project database, oad), from a table file or from any column table; checked by alidate; enerate derives the tables the model's sources read — the sub-block kits, the block orders and the erection plan — so the three always agree. Every column becomes an item label. Columns (names are case-insensitive): block , sub (required); kind , turn (0 / 1), length , breadth , depth (m), weight (t), erect_seq , erect_after (blocks erected first, separated by spaces, commas or semicolons), hull_x / hull_y / hull_z (m), any t_<stage> (work content, model time units); other columns are carried as labels. class ErectionDock A slipway or building dock: it erects ship blocks and keeps them — the hull. Which block it takes : under rectionRule.Sequence only the next block of the erection sequence (its…

SimuLean.Naval  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Naval/ErectionDock.cs:29

: Element, IWorkStation, IResourceUser, IKeepsItems

A slipway or building dock: it erects ship blocks and keeps them — the hull. Which block it takes : under rectionRule.Sequence only the next block of the erection sequence (its erect_seq label = the number of blocks started + 1); under rectionRule.Precedence any block whose erect_after blocks are all erected — several erection fronts at once, up to apacity. A block it cannot take yet is refused (upstream keeps it: a yard releasing any accepted item or a list lets the others pass), and the dock asks again after every erection. Erection : the time of its sampler (an expression may read the block's labels, e.g. 2 + 0.05 * weight ), with its process resources (crane, erection crew; their own share with processHoldFor ), on its own front; stops pause it as every station's work. The hull : an erected block stays (at rest, KeepsItems). With xpectedBlocks set, the complete hull leaves as one ship item (the blocks as its sub-items, each counted as leaving) to the dock's output — a launch / float-out sink — and the dock starts the next hull. Without an output (or with xpectedBlocks = 0) the hull stays and the makespan is the last erection. Flow statistics come from the link layer: a block enters when the dock takes it.

class ParameterSchema What the keys of a config mean for parameterisation — declared once per element type (its handler's imuLean.Serialization.IElementHandler.Schema), for resource teams and for downtimes.…

SimuLean.Optimization  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Optimization/ParameterSchema.cs:15

What the keys of a config mean for parameterisation — declared once per element type (its handler's imuLean.Serialization.IElementHandler.Schema), for resource teams and for downtimes. Numbers, bools and number arrays need no declaration (their type says it); a text or a list must be declared: an option (hoice), a sampler spec Type~p1~p2 (ampler), numbers in a text a|b|c (umberList), a list of numbers (umbers) — or tructural (names, references, tables, expressions: not a parameter). A key left undecided fails the catalog test, so a new element type, key or property is offered — or deliberately not — from the start.

Kinematic travel by axes (gantry cranes, AS/RS cranes, robots): between the coordinates of two locations (points of a ransportNetwork; tracks are not used), each axis x / y / z moves its distance with a trapezoidal profile — max speed, acceleration (0 = instant) — and the axes move together (time = the slowest axis) or one after the other (time = the sum). An axis with speed 0 does not move (a distance on it is unreachable). istance is the travel time (the cost "nearest" rules compare).

class ResourceDispatcher The element that hands resources out ("elemento ordenador"): its members — any askExecutors, operators, tools, vehicles — wait in a esources list while free, and esourceRequests wait in…

SimuLean.Resources  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Resources/ResourceDispatcher.cs:20

: IWarmupStatistics

The element that hands resources out ("elemento ordenador"): its members — any askExecutors, operators, tools, vehicles — wait in a esources list while free, and esourceRequests wait in a equests list. Both are ordinary imLists, so the priority rule is a pair of list orders (and user fields / formulas): equestOrder decides which request is served first, esourceOrder which free resource it gets. No rule = FIFO if available : requests in arrival order, resources in the order they became free (longest idle first). Dispatching runs whenever a request arrives or a member becomes free: requests are tried in order; one is served only if all its requirements can be met at once (all-or-nothing: no partial holds, no deadlock); a request that cannot be served yet does not block the ones behind it. The two lists keep their statistics (request waiting time = time waiting for resources).

class ResourceRequest A request for resources made to a esourceDispatcher by an element (a station, a transport request). It waits in the dispatcher's request list until all its requirements can be met at…

SimuLean.Resources  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Resources/ResourceRequest.cs:40

: IListFieldSource

A request for resources made to a esourceDispatcher by an element (a station, a transport request). It waits in the dispatcher's request list until all its requirements can be met at once; then nAssigned receives the resources and must give each a task (askExecutor.Execute) — resources left without a task go back to the dispatcher. The resources are released when their tasks end (the task type decides where: transport at the unload, setup / process at their end, or after a Hold ). List fields (for request-order rules): priority , requestTime , count (resources needed), text station (requester name), taskType , skill (the first requirement's label); plus age from the list, and user fields of the list.

class ResourceTransportLink Output link of an element whose items are carried by resources (operators, vehicles) to the next elements — the "transport" use of a resource, next to "process". Abstract carriers take a…

SimuLean.Resources  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Resources/ResourceTransportLink.cs:23

: ILink

Output link of an element whose items are carried by resources (operators, vehicles) to the next elements — the "transport" use of a resource, next to "process". Abstract carriers take a transport time per move; spatial carriers (vehicles on the network) first travel empty to the origin's lement.Location, load, travel to the destination's location with their travel model (unless ravelTime is set) and unload. When the origin offers an item, a destination with room is chosen (the origin's output strategy among the destinations that can take it, counting the items already on their way to each), a transport request is made to the dispatcher and the origin keeps the item (refused send → BLOCKED, as with a full destination). When a resource is assigned it loads the item: the origin hands it over (lement.SendHeldItem) and the item leaves it ( OnExit ); it travels for the transport time, unloads and delivers it to the destination ( Receive , OnEntry ) — statistics stay link-driven. If the destination cannot take it then (another element filled it), the resource waits, HELD, until it can. Resources are released at the delivery (task type Transport).

class TrafficControl Traffic on a ransportNetwork: every track (either direction — two vehicles cannot pass on it) holds at most egmentCapacity vehicles. A vehicle reserves the next segment before entering…

SimuLean.Resources  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Resources/Traffic.cs:27

Traffic on a ransportNetwork: every track (either direction — two vehicles cannot pass on it) holds at most egmentCapacity vehicles. A vehicle reserves the next segment before entering it, keeps the one it is on while it waits at the node (as a real vehicle does), and enters a released segment in arrival order. Shared by every team travelling on the network; one per model run (eset at start). Deadlocks (a cycle of vehicles each waiting for a segment the next one holds — e.g. two vehicles meeting head-on) are detected when a vehicle starts waiting, by following the wait chain; the vehicle closing the cycle is let through (the segment goes over its capacity for it) and the event is counted (eadlocksResolved) — a model with many of them needs passing places or one-way tracks.

enum ChartKind The kinds of chart.

SimuLean.Results.Charts  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Results/Charts/ChartQuery.cs:7

The kinds of chart.

Values

BarMean per category with its confidence interval across replications.
BoxDistribution per category across replications: min, quartiles, median, max.
HistogramCounts of the values in bins.
ScatterOne point per run: X against Y (e.g. a parameter against a metric).
LineA recorded time series: one line per run and object.
StatesShare of time per state, stacked per object.
StackedStacked columns (e.g. per period of a live run), absolute or each column to 100 % (hartData.Normalise). Drawn from data built in code (the element inspector, dashboards), not from a query.
GanttA Gantt of one run: a row per object, its state intervals over time in the states' colours (needs the run's timeline: Record timeline).
JobGanttA job Gantt of one run: a row per item, where it was over time (a colour per element; needs Record timeline).
AreaThe first series as a filled area, the others as lines, one column per category (e.g. content: mean and max per time bucket). Drawn from data built in code, not from a query.

class SeriesRecorder Records time series of a headless run without touching the model: it advances the clock interval by interval (imClock.AdvanceClock runs every event up to each boundary, so the run is the…

SimuLean.Results  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Results/TimeSeries.cs:48

Records time series of a headless run without touching the model: it advances the clock interval by interval (imClock.AdvanceClock runs every event up to each boundary, so the run is the same as one call) and at each boundary reads the cumulative statistics, keeping their change over the interval: elements — input , output (items in the interval), content (at the end), content_avg (time-weighted over the interval), state:X (share of the interval); resources — utilization and state:X (share of the interval); lists — content , content_avg , pushed , pulled . With a warm-up the series start at the end of the warm-up (the statistics are reset there).

A TrueType font read and rasterised by the engine, so charts get real typography without Unity: the cmap (formats 4 and 12), head , hhea , hmtx , maxp , loca and glyf tables (simple and composite glyphs, quadratic outlines). Glyphs are drawn by exact area coverage (an accumulation rasteriser: anti-aliased, non-zero filling of non-overlapping outlines) and cached per size and quarter-pixel position. No hinting, no kerning (Inter's spacing is good without). Thread-safe.

class Reaction "When [elements] [signal] if [condition] do [actions]": subscribes to a signal of its source elements in the model's ignalHub and, each time the signal passes its state filter and…

: ISignalSink, IWarmupStatistics

"When [elements] [signal] if [condition] do [actions]": subscribes to a signal of its source elements in the model's ignalHub and, each time the signal passes its state filter and condition, runs its actions in order (each with its optional "only if"). Several reactions on one signal run in the order they were built. Expressions see the signal's item and element ( item.x , element.content , get('E', 'p') , data tables); random functions draw from the reaction's own stream. Counts what it did (the Play inspector shows it). A failing action stops the run with an error naming the reaction.

class DistributionFitter static Fits the SimuLean catalog's distributions to a sample: closed-form maximum likelihood (Exponential, Normal, LogNormal, Uniform, Poisson), Newton maximum likelihood (Gamma, Weibull — with…

SimuLean.Stochastics.Fitting  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Stochastics/Fitting/DistributionFitter.cs:46

Fits the SimuLean catalog's distributions to a sample: closed-form maximum likelihood (Exponential, Normal, LogNormal, Uniform, Poisson), Newton maximum likelihood (Gamma, Weibull — with Probability's digamma / trigamma), moments (Triangular, Beta on the data's range, Binomial), the range (discrete uniform); each candidate's Kolmogorov–Smirnov and Anderson–Darling statistics with p-values, χ² by classes, log-likelihood and AIC; ranked by the chosen criterion — for integer (count) data by the χ² p-value instead, KS / AD being for continuous distributions. The p-values are for a fully specified distribution: with estimated parameters they are optimistic (a "good" verdict is a necessary, not a sufficient, condition). Families the data cannot have (a positive family for negative data, a discrete one for non-integer data) are skipped.

class Probability static Probability functions of SimuLean (D1, they replaced ALGLIB): CDFs, quantiles and probability masses of the distributions, and the functions behind them — Γ, ln Γ, B, the regularized…

SimuLean.Stochastics  ·  Assets/SimuLean.Net/Stochastics/Probability/Probability.cs:15

Probability functions of SimuLean (D1, they replaced ALGLIB): CDFs, quantiles and probability masses of the distributions, and the functions behind them — Γ, ln Γ, B, the regularized incomplete gamma and beta and their inverses, erf / erfc. Every quantile is the inverse of its CDF (x with CDF(x) = p). Written from the published algorithms: ln Γ by Lanczos' approximation (g = 7, 9 terms) with reflection below 1/2; the incomplete gamma by its series (x < a + 1) or Legendre's continued fraction (modified Lentz); the incomplete beta by its continued fraction (Lentz) with I_x(a, b) = 1 − I_(1−x)(b, a); erf x = P(1/2, x²); the normal quantile by Acklam's approximation refined with Halley steps; the inverses by Newton / Halley steps kept inside a bracket. Checked against ALGLIB 4.07 on a grid, tails included ( StandaloneTests/probabilitytests ).

Baseline = JSON object: model , elements (count), connections (count) and stats : element id → { metric → value }. Structural differences (element / connection counts, missing elements or metrics) always fail; numbers are compared with a relative tolerance.

Reference models of the regression net. Each is a small, single-purpose imulationConfig built with the same DTOs and handler type names the scene extractor emits, so one definition serves the headless runner ( StandaloneTests/referencemodels ), the Unity EditMode tests and, later, a scene generator. Every model has a fixed seed and horizon: results are deterministic and are compared with the stored baselines by eferenceModelRunner. Engine-pure (no Unity types).

SimulationConfig CombinerStarved()statica welding cell (Combiner, 1 kit per block) and a prep station share one welder, who walks between them. While the cell waits for the welder it already takes the kit of its next block (the components of the next job). 2 blocks and 4 kits (through a rack of 5): when the 2nd block is out, the cell holds the kit it took for a 3rd block that will never come (the block source is exhausted) and the rack another. No material: the run is finished (starved), not a deadlock, and the cell is reported waiting for its main input.

SimulationConfig EndAtStorage()staticThe same yard ended by the hull instead (#27): stop when the two hull queues have received the 4 blocks.
SimulationConfig EndWhenEmpty()static300 scheduled items through a server; the run ends when the model is empty, long before its horizon.
SimulationConfig ErectionPrecedence()staticErection by precedence: block 1 first, 2 and 3 on it, 4 on 2, 5 on 3, 6 on 4 and 5; two erection fronts, a constant erection time and an erection crew of two; no launch — the hull stays in the dock (terminal: the makespan is its last erection).
SimulationConfig ErectionSequence()staticErection in sequence: six blocks arrive out of order into a yard that releases any accepted item; the slipway takes only the next of the sequence (one front), the erection time grows with the block's weight, the crane is held only for its lift (`processHoldFor`); the complete hull leaves as one ship to a launch sink that keeps it.
SimulationConfig FinishWithSurplus()static4 scheduled blocks assembled with a kit each from an unlimited kit source through a rack of 3, into the "hull": two queues of 2 without outputs (no sink). When the 4th block is in, the kit source is blocked behind the full rack and nothing will take the kits: the run is finished (surplus, not a deadlock), ends there ("when empty"), and its makespan is the last entry into the hull.
SimulationConfig LengthLimitedLanes()staticSource → a two-lane accumulation buffer limited by length (lanes 6 and 4, gap 0.5, items 1 or 2.5 long by their length label) → Server → Sink (R-11).
SimulationConfig ListCombiner()staticCombiner whose main input is a connection and whose component input pulls from a list fed by two queues (source labels prio 1 / 5, highest first): inputOrder placeholder + port.
SimulationConfig ListFilteredPull()staticOne queue pushes items of kind 1 / 2 to a list; each server pulls only its kind.
SimulationConfig ListPriorityDispatch()staticTwo queues push their items (labels prio 1 or 5) to the list work ; two servers pull the highest priority first (list default order): a model-wide priority queue.
SimulationConfig MultiServer3()staticSource → Queue → MultiServer(3) → Sink: parallel slots.
SimulationConfig NavalBlockProcess()staticThe naval library's block process (N3, the IJPR 2025 flow on existing elements, generic data): sub-block kits -> sub-assembly (2 cells, fitters) -> turning when the sub-block is turned -> sub-block yard (any accepted) -> block assembly bays (Combiner, 2 in parallel, block = its nsub sub-blocks, welders) -> outfitting -> blasting and painting (the painter for 6 of its 10 h: processHoldFor) -> block yard -> slipway (sequence, crane for the lift only) -> launch (keeps the ship). The tables are the sample hull's generated parts.
SimulationConfig OperatorPoolModel()staticTwo servers sharing one operator (a team of one, kept until the item leaves): WAITING_FOR_RESOURCE.
SimulationConfig PickingModel()staticContainers pick 2 units from a stock port; surplus returns to a sink.
SimulationConfig ResourceAgvTraffic()staticresource_fleet_nearest with three AGVs under traffic control on its single-lane line: they queue behind each other, meet head-on (deadlocks resolved) and wait at nodes.
SimulationConfig ResourceCountTwo()staticA job needing two operators (all-or-nothing) next to jobs needing one, from a team of three.
SimulationConfig ResourceFleetNearest()staticTwo origins at the ends of a line (A — D — B, 25 m each) send to a dock D; a fleet of two AGVs takes the nearest free vehicle (resource order distance ) — vehicles wait for work where they unloaded.
SimulationConfig ResourceGantryStacker()staticA stacker whose cycles a gantry crane does (axes x / y / z): pick point K, two stacks.
SimulationConfig ResourceRequestPriority()staticTwo stations share one operator; requests are served by the item's prio label.
SimulationConfig ResourceRobotCell()staticA robot on axes (with acceleration) carries between two machines of a cell.
SimulationConfig ResourceSharedTeam()staticReference model: three stations share a team of two operators; a slow station behind them makes them block, and an operator stays with a blocked station until its item leaves (the process task's "hold until the item leaves" option).
SimulationConfig ResourceSkillQuery()staticTwo lines (welding, painting) served by one crew: members carry skill labels, each station asks for its skill, and among the qualified members the least used one is taken (resource order).
SimulationConfig ResourceTransport()staticA crew both processes at a station and carries its items to the next station (load + travel + unload); the destination queue is small, so moves wait for room.
SimulationConfig ResourceWalkCalibrated()staticresource_walk_matrix with travel times calibrated (as if measured with Unity physics): the matrix is the estimate, some pairs have their own observed means, the rest the general model.
SimulationConfig ResourceWalkGrid()staticOperators walking freely on a walk grid (A*) around a wall between two stations: they process at both and carry from the first to the second (nearest operator).
SimulationConfig ResourceWalkMatrix()staticTwo operators walking on a distance matrix: they walk to station m1 or m2 to process (resource order distance = the nearest), and carry m1's items to m2.
SimulationConfig RoutingRoundRobin()staticSource → 2 servers (round robin) → Sink: output-strategy routing.
SimuLean.Naval.BlockBreakdown SampleHull()staticA generic sample hull for the naval library (no yard data): 4 blocks, 7 sub-blocks, block 1 first, 2 and 3 on it, 4 on both; the work content per stage in hours (t_sba, t_ba).
SimulationConfig ShiftModel()staticOne week in minutes from Monday 2026-10-05 00:00; the server works Mon–Fri 06:00–14:00 (a shift downtime, 40 h of 168 h), arrivals all week (R-11).
SimulationConfig StackerModel()staticStacker with 2 positions of 4: compound release and stacking statistics.
SimulationConfig StallCombiner()staticA Combiner needs 2 components per main item: 3 mains and 4 components, so the third main waits forever — the run stalls (nothing blocked: a starved kit); flagged, and the run goes on to its horizon.
SimulationConfig TransportModel()staticSource → queue at node n1 ⇒ an AGV (team on the network, 10 m at 1 m/s, load / unload 1) ⇒ queue at node n2 → Sink: vehicle transport through the dispatcher (travel empty, load, travel, unload).
SimulationConfig WalkingPatients()staticPatients that walk by themselves (WalkLink): they enter at the door, walk 15 m to a waiting area of three, 10 m to the consultation and 15 m to the exit at 1.2 m/s (time unit 1 s), between the network's nodes.
SimulationConfig WarmupModel()staticMulti-server model with a warm-up: statistics cover [500, 2500] only.
SimulationConfig YardKitting(string release = "AnyAccepted")staticA yard (buffer of 4) serves two assembly bays by key: each bay (a Combiner, pull mode SingleLabel on block with no value = its main item's block) takes the sub-block of its own block; a crane (team crane , the yard's transport) carries each sub-block. Sub-blocks arrive 1, 2, 3, 4, but bay A builds block 3 first, then 1 (out of order). release AnyAccepted: the yard offers every held sub-block (FIFO would deadlock: block 1 at the head, wanted by nobody yet).
SimulationConfig YardKittingCapacity()staticOne bay area with two assemblies in parallel (Combiner capacity 2) instead of two bays: each assembly matches its own main item; the blocks arrive 3, 1, 2, 4 and the sub-blocks 1, 2, 3, 4.
SimulationConfig YardKittingList()staticThe yard as a list (kitting by key through a list): the bays pull "the sub-block of my block"; the crane is the yard's transport (the holder's, as FlexSim's Use Transport ).
SimulationConfig YardListAxes()staticthe yard serves sub-blocks by key ( block ) to 2 bays through a list, and an overhead crane on axes (team travel Axes , real durations from the points' coordinates) carries each one from the yard to the bay that pulled it. Out-of-order blocks: bay A builds 3 then 1, bay B 2 then 4; the sub-blocks arrive 1, 2, 3, 4.
SimulationConfig YardListDeadlock()statica real deadlock through a list. The yard (capacity 1) pushes its sub-blocks to a list; two bays (Combiners, SingleLabel on block ) hold blocks 3 and 2 and pull "the sub-block of my block" from it. Sub-block 1 arrives first, fills the yard and nobody wants it: the yard waits for the list's pullers, the bays wait for their components from the list, the sub-blocks' source is blocked behind the yard.
